original_question: Let C be a simple planar convex curve contained in a plane P, let D be the planar domain bounded by C, and let Sigma be a compact constant-mean-curvature surface spanning C. If Sigma is contained in D x R, must Sigma be a graph on D?
target_in_paper: Section 3 (Part II: Arbitrary boundary curve), Problem 3.6 (3*)
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's exact target. It has the right geometric setting (a simple planar convex curve C in a plane P, the bounded domain D enclosed by C, a compact constant-mean-curvature surface spanning C, and the inclusion in D x R), and it asks exactly the same conclusion as the paper: whether the surface must be a graph on D.
missing_details: The ambient manifold should be stated explicitly as Euclidean three-space R^3.
To match the paper's notation, 'spanning C' should be unpacked as: there is an immersion Psi: Sigma -> R^3 whose boundary map Psi|_{∂Sigma}: ∂Sigma -> C is a diffeomorphism.
Because the paper fixes coordinates so that P is horizontal, the set D x R means the vertical solid cylinder over D; without that coordinate choice, this notation is not literally defined.
For full stand-alone precision, 'graph on D' should mean a single-valued graph over D with respect to orthogonal projection onto P.
The problem is asked with no extra assumptions such as embeddedness, disk-type, stability, or small mean curvature; those are deliberately not part of the hypothesis.
If one wants every hidden assumption visible, C should be described as a simple closed convex planar curve, since D is the bounded domain enclosed by C.
The paper does not exclude the minimal case H = 0, although the introduction notes that for planar boundary this case is trivial.
refined_question: Let Psi: Sigma -> R^3 be an isometric immersion of a compact surface with nonempty boundary and constant mean curvature, and assume that Psi|_{∂Sigma}: ∂Sigma -> C is a diffeomorphism onto a simple closed convex curve C contained in a plane P. Let D subset P be the bounded domain enclosed by C. After a rigid motion sending P to a horizontal plane, assume that Psi(Sigma) is contained in the vertical cylinder D x R over D. Without any further hypotheses such as embeddedness or disk-type, must Psi(Sigma) be a single-valued graph over D with respect to orthogonal projection onto P?
justification: The draft clearly targets the arbitrary-boundary problem in Section 3, not the opening circle-boundary conjectures. Problem 3.6 states this question almost verbatim. The only real incompleteness is that the paper's notation makes several assumptions implicit: surfaces live in R^3, 'spanning C' is defined via an immersion whose boundary map is a diffeomorphism onto C, and P is taken horizontal so that D x R denotes the vertical cylinder over D. The paragraph immediately after Problem 3.6 gives the nearby scope-setting facts: embeddedness already implies the graph conclusion, and if an H-graph on D exists for the same H, then any such surface agrees with it up to reflection; these are contextual partial results, not alternate formulations of the same open problem.
